Key observations from test image:
- Several soybean plants have collapsed/died in a patch
- Brown, dead stems visible in center with surrounding healthy green plants
- Dead leaves remain attached to stems
- Some whitish/pale appearance on dying stems
- Pods are visible on plants
- Stem-level disease causing plant death

Top candidates: **White_Mold** (dead leaves stay attached, white growth on stems), **Phytophthora** (stem collapse, plant death), **Rhizoctonia**. Let me check references.

**Analysis:**

- **Test image**: Patch of dying/dead soybean plants collapsed together, brown stems, dead leaves remaining attached to stems, healthy green plants surrounding the dying patch, pods visible
- **White_Mold ref**: Shows white fluffy mycelium with characteristic black sclerotia on stems — no clear white mycelium or sclerotia visible in test image
- **Phytophthora ref**: Shows wilting/dying plants with dead leaves hanging, brown stems, surrounded by healthy plants — **strong visual match** to test image
- **Rhizoctonia ref**: Close-up of single stem with reddish-brown canker at soil line — different presentation

The test image pattern — multiple plants dying in a patch, dead leaves remaining attached, brown wilted stems, plants collapsed while neighbors remain healthy — is the classic field appearance of **Phytophthora** root and stem rot.
